action: Read the home page.

action: Change Show prices in to each option in turn.

action: Look for anything about tax.

action: Look for how to cancel.
expected: It says cancelling is done in the host dashboard, and that the wall keeps working until the end of the period already paid for.

action: Read both pages for promises.
expected: No promise of more bookings, higher star ratings, more reviews, more money, less damage or cleaner guests, and no claim of a link with Airbnb, Booking.com or similar.

action: Click Add a memory, type a short message, tick the consent box and press Continue.

action: Scroll to the very bottom.

action: Open the same demo pages on your phone.
expected: They fit the screen without scrolling sideways.

action: At the bottom of the home page click Privacy & Safety.

action: Look at what the form asks for.
expected: Request type (Privacy request, Content takedown, Urgent safety concern), Details and Contact email. Nothing unrelated.

action: Test site only Choose Privacy request. In Details type “TEST, please ignore. Tester check TP-PUB-02”. Enter your test inbox address and press Submit request.

action: From the links at the bottom of the page, open Terms and then Privacy.

action: Click Host sign in, then Create a host account.

action: Before typing anything, read the line under Password.

action: Not built yet Look for a tick box about marketing emails or news.

action: Not built yet Look for links to the Terms and the Privacy Policy.

action: Fill it in properly and press Create account.

action: Click Sign out, then sign back in with the same email and password.

action: On a test property without a stored review preference, submit a fully clear memory. Then turn Review content before publication on and submit another clear memory.

action: As the unrelated host and as a signed-out visitor, try changing the setting through the UI and backend. As the owner, save the setting and reload.
expected: Only the owner can change it. The saved value persists. Unauthorised calls cannot change the property's review policy.

action: With review off, submit separate clear-scanned memories containing an email address, phone number and external link. Also submit ordinary profanity without serious flags.
expected: Each memory waits for host review despite review being off. Contact detection does not clear a failed provider scan or override a serious flag. Private feedback with ordinary complaints/contact details remains private and follows its own screening rules.

action: With clear and ordinary memories waiting, turn review off. Turn it on again after a different clear memory has already published.
expected: Turning review off does not bulk-publish existing waiting items. Turning it on does not retroactively hide published memories. Approve waiting items individually.

action: Approve one ordinary-held memory and reject another. Repeat with a clear memory held only by the review switch. Check both walls, submission status and photo access.
expected: Only an eligible current revision can be approved. Approved memories become visible; rejected memories remain off the walls and public photo access is denied. Record the actual rejection/deletion policy without assuming immediate object deletion.

action: Attempt approval with a stale revision, an open report, a safety hold and an offline property, using separate fixtures. Attempt approval as another host.
expected: Each unsafe or unauthorised approval is refused. Refreshing or changing the switch does not bypass the report, revision, safety or property checks.

action: For an ordinary held memory, check the notification outbox and, where configured, the test host email inbox.
expected: The hold is recorded once for that revision. Record outbox creation and actual email receipt separately; a queued notification is not proof of delivery.

action: As a signed-out user, ordinary host, unrelated host and operations account without MFA, try opening case messages, reading individual case photos and resolving each case through both UI and direct backend calls.
expected: All attempts are denied. Restricted text and photos are absent from ordinary host/public views and exports. Hiding UI controls alone does not count as access denial.

action: As an authorised operations admin with MFA, open a memory case and each individual photo, then a private-feedback case. Inspect the audit trail.
expected: Authorised content is readable. Each message/case opening and photo opening records actor, case reference, action and timestamp. Audit/log records do not copy the message or photo bytes; photo delivery does not issue permanent public download tokens.

action: Release an unchanged memory case to the host. Repeat with host review switched off.
expected: The safety hold clears and the memory enters ordinary host review. Release does not publish it, even with review off. The case is resolved, restricted references are cleared, and the decision is audited.

action: Edit a memory while it is safety-held, then release the old case. Also try approving or resolving a stale revision.
expected: Release queues the current changed revision for fresh screening rather than approving the old content. Stale decisions cannot publish it. A new serious result reopens the appropriate restricted case; other results follow the current policy.

action: Release a private-feedback case, then delete a separate feedback case. Try releasing feedback after its property has been removed.
expected: Released feedback reaches only the owning host inbox once. Deleted feedback is not delivered and its restricted message is cleared. A case whose property no longer exists cannot be released. Decisions are audited.

action: Delete a memory case. Inspect the post, submission, case, both photo buckets and the deletion job; run the authorised deletion worker on the test environment.
expected: The memory is hidden, message cleared and case references removed. Deletion is queued for quarantine and delivery objects with the existing 72-hour due date. Record actual removal of every object separately from job creation; backup/recovery retention is a separate check.

action: As the guest, withdraw a safety-held memory. Try releasing it, then resolve the hold by deletion through operations.
expected: Withdrawal hides it immediately. It cannot be released. Operations deletion resolves the safety hold so scheduled object deletion can proceed; it never republishes the withdrawn memory.

action: After release or deletion, retry every saved case-photo request. Race a photo read against case resolution; repeat a resolution action.
expected: New requests and reads whose state recheck sees resolution are denied. Repeat resolution cannot deliver twice. Previously downloaded external copies cannot be revoked and are not evidence of endpoint access after resolution.

action: Request photo delivery before screening completes, during host review and during a restricted safety hold. Try anonymous direct bucket URLs and saved storage/object references.
expected: The application refuses public photo delivery for all unpublished states. Guest-photo buckets deny unauthorised direct access; a known object path does not bypass application checks.

action: For a published visible memory on an active property, load its application photo endpoint. Then separately hide the post, remove it, open a safety restriction and take the property offline; retry the saved endpoint after each change.
expected: The valid published photo is served. Each state change prevents new delivery. Check both public and in-stay pages; endpoint denial is verified directly rather than inferred only from disappearing UI.

action: Have engineering change submission revision/status, post visibility or property availability while the endpoint is retrieving a photo.
expected: The final state recheck denies delivery when status/revision/visibility/availability has changed. Publication checks are repeated before bytes are sent.

action: Edit a published memory and let it enter pending screening. Complete clear, ordinary-held and serious-held scans in separate cases.
expected: The edited revision stays off the wall until its current scan completes. The old result cannot restore it. Each final result follows the review setting and safety/report checks; old saved photo requests do not bypass the pending state.

action: Open a guest report or safety hold while a scan/approval is finishing, then attempt dismissal/restoration while another report or hold remains.
expected: A concurrent report or hold prevents publication/restoration. Dismissing one report cannot override another open report or restricted case. Record final state and saved-endpoint access.

action: Inspect successful photo response headers and attempt invalid IDs and out-of-range photo indexes.
expected: Photo responses specify private, no-store caching. Invalid requests return no photo or private record details. Record the limits of previously downloaded/cached external copies separately from new endpoint requests.

action: Before calling Google, have the owner/reviewer label each fixture's intended route independently. Include clear text, ordinary profanity/complaints, all four serious text categories, slang/misspellings, quoted or reported incidents, benign historical references and mixed serious/ordinary signals. Use both text routes.
expected: Fixture IDs, intended routes, language/context and review rationale are recorded before provider scores are known. Confidence describes category confidence, not swear-word severity. Missing fixture coverage is recorded as blocked.

action: Prepare representative photo fixtures for adult, violence, medical, racy, spoof, benign swimwear/medical contexts and mixed multi-photo submissions. Use lawful approved synthetic or licensed examples; do not use real guest photos or illegal material.
expected: Each intended route is documented. This checks calibration of the provisional likelihood mapping, not age, consent, legality or comprehensive detection. Text/contact details embedded in photos remain a separately documented detection gap.

action: Submit every approved fixture to real Google screening through the application. Record submission/revision, screening reference, provider categories/scores/likelihoods, final route and elapsed time.
expected: Observed application routing matches the actual provider result and configured rules. Record a missed harmful classification or benign false positive even when the application correctly follows that score. Do not fabricate scores to make a real-provider test pass.

action: Compare observed classifications with the independent intended routes. Count and review false positives, false negatives and uncertain cases for each route/category/context with the owner and safety reviewer.
expected: The calibration report records discrepancies, proposed threshold/wording changes and a dated owner decision. Acceptance criteria and minimum sample coverage are agreed before declaring calibration passed. A small successful sample is not a guarantee of detecting all harmful content.

action: On both real phones, follow a clear memory with review off, a clear memory with review on, an ordinary-held memory and a serious-held memory from submission through host or safety review. Follow clear/ordinary feedback delivery and serious feedback release/deletion.
expected: Record separate phone/browser results and complete journeys: guest confirmation, wall/inbox visibility, appropriate reviewer access, decisions and final photo access. Provider connectivity alone does not prove any complete journey.

action: Check runtime provider endpoint diagnostics, notification receipt, reviewer MFA/access, staff ownership and the deletion follow-up for the real-provider run.
expected: Configured regional endpoints, actual notification receipt, successful authorised review and object-removal evidence are recorded separately. Missing staffing, email or deletion evidence stays outstanding even if routing passes.

action: Create a result row per fixture/route/device with expected outcome, actual outcome, pass/fail/blocked, evidence location and reviewer decision. Clean up test submissions using their normal deletion workflows.
expected: Routing tests, real-provider calibration, device results and operational evidence each have their own outcomes. Documented steps or an earlier build/test count are not recorded as a pass. Owner reviews remaining gaps before broader intake; legal approval remains a separate release condition.

expected: Refused: it says access needs an authorised operations account. No queues or data are shown.

action: Sign out and try the same address.
expected: You are asked to sign in. Nothing is shown.

action: Create a test property and contribution under each account. Record both property IDs.
expected: Each account sees only its own dashboard, properties, feedback and host review items.

action: As the other host, open the first property URL and attempt to read or change it. Repeat with the accounts swapped.
expected: The server refuses cross-account reads and writes. No private content is returned.

action: Open each property guest link in separate guest sessions; try a contribution or photo reference from the other property.
expected: The session cannot contribute to or access restricted content belonging to the other property.

action: Try the photo endpoint and copied storage URL while signed out, as the other host and as an unrelated guest.
expected: Quarantine, host-review and safety-held photos remain inaccessible. Private feedback never appears in public responses.

action: Publish an approved test photo and confirm it displays through the application; then hide it and repeat the same photo request.
expected: The published photo displays; hiding it blocks subsequent direct requests. Record the URL, time and response status; an old browser screenshot is not proof of current access.

action: Check host exports and the public wall for held content and private feedback.
expected: Restricted content and private feedback are absent from ordinary public views and host exports.

action: Submit a memory whose text/photo screening cannot complete; repeat for private feedback. Record submission and case IDs.
expected: Each opens restricted safety review tagged Screening incomplete. The reviewer sees the reason. Memory stays unpublished; feedback stays undelivered.

action: Attempt host approval, public photo access and ordinary-host case access.
expected: All bypass attempts are refused; the host cannot open the restricted case.

action: Retry after provider recovery, and edit the held memory without resolving its case.
expected: An open case still prevents automatic publication or feedback delivery. A retry cannot silently clear it.

action: Use the authorised MFA reviewer to release the case.
expected: An unchanged memory goes to host review; an edited memory is screened again; released feedback reaches only the private inbox. Record the audit and destination.

action: Record how the failure was produced.
expected: A scoped injected failure proves failure routing only. A real Google result is required for provider classification evidence.

action: Submit clear memories with the host-review switch off and on. Submit an ordinary flagged memory and a memory with contact details or a link.
expected: Clear memories publish with review off and wait for host approval with review on. Ordinary flags and screened contact details/links enter host review.

action: Send clear and ordinary private feedback, then submit authorised serious-text and serious-photo examples.
expected: Ordinary feedback reaches the private inbox. Serious text and serious-photo results enter restricted safety review. Record the actual provider categories and resulting route; do not rely on fixture labels alone.

action: Sign in as a normal host, an authorised reviewer without MFA and an authorised reviewer with MFA. Open a restricted case and its photos.
expected: Only the authorised reviewer signed in with MFA can access case data. A Google-account security setting alone is not evidence of Firebase MFA. Local reviewer simulation does not satisfy this live check.

action: Release and delete separate disposable cases, and try the same resolution twice.
expected: Release follows the agreed destination; deletion hides the content and schedules photo removal. Actions are audited and cannot resurrect deleted content or apply a second conflicting resolution.

action: Open the guest link or QR code on each device, submit a message/photo, edit and delete it, and send separate private feedback.
expected: The journeys complete with clear acknowledgements, correct privacy and no host interface exposed to guests.

action: Try ten permitted images, an extra image, oversized/unsupported files and an iPhone HEIC selection. Interrupt an upload and retry it.
expected: Limits are enforced with clear recovery messages and no duplicate submission. Record the observed HEIC handling and any device issue.

action: Use keyboard navigation on desktop and check small screens, consent and error messages.
expected: Controls remain reachable and readable; required memory consent is enforced. Mark unavailable physical-device checks blocked rather than claiming a pass.

action: Delete a test memory with photos; repeat for a memory held in safety review.
expected: The contribution immediately disappears from public views and direct photo requests. The correct deletion job lists its objects.

action: After the deletion worker runs, verify the submission state and every listed object in the live storage buckets.
expected: Every targeted live object is absent. A queued job, hidden post or local test result alone is not deletion proof. Record timestamps and evidence.

action: Check feedback removal, retained consent/audit records and any recoverable or backup copies against section 5.10.
expected: The report identifies what was deleted, what remains and why. Live-object deletion is distinguished from soft deletion, recovery and backup retention.

action: Before any wider cleanup, list the dedicated account/property IDs and the exact records/files to remove.
expected: Cleanup stays within the approved test scope. No customer data or test account/property is deleted merely because this check passed.

action: The owner configures the 50c price for the selected dedicated test account/property. Record the property and Stripe price/subscription references.
expected: The test configuration is identifiable and scoped to the test property/account. Its currency and billing interval are recorded; the ordinary published prices remain separately documented.

action: Open live checkout for that property and inspect the total and whether payment is immediate or follows a trial.
expected: The intended 50c amount, currency, any tax and charge date are clearly shown. If checkout differs from the agreed test setup, mark it blocked and correct the setup before paying.

action: Complete the agreed live payment journey, where payment is needed, and return to the property.
expected: Record the actual Stripe charge/invoice and the resulting property state. A successful redirect alone is not payment or webhook proof. If no charge occurs during a trial, record that accurately; do not claim a paid checkout passed.

action: Cancel a test subscription and separately cancel a test trial where available. Record the subscription state, next charge and access end date.
expected: The dashboard and Stripe subscription agree on cancellation and any scheduled end date. The trial cancellation shows whether a future charge is prevented. Record observations; future renewal prevention is not proved by a button click alone.

action: If testing the restore/keep-subscription control, restore once and then cancel again so the final state is clear.
expected: The resulting subscription, charge schedule and property access match the UI. Record the final state and any real charge; do not leave an unintended renewal active.

action: Enter the results and evidence in the shared NAS register, using Mobile/Desktop and Pass/Fail for each step.
expected: Live payments, cancellation, any refund and any outstanding checks are recorded separately. A cancellation is not recorded as a refund without refund evidence. No account/property cleanup occurs as part of this check.

action: Developer: check the live Firebase project uses Authentication with Identity Platform, then enable authenticator-app MFA using the documented project configuration method.
expected: Record the project and enabled configuration. This enables the capability; it does not enrol the reviewer.

action: Owner/developer: select the reviewer account, verify its email and arrange its authorised operations role.
expected: The correct account is authorised for operations. Ordinary test-host accounts remain ordinary hosts.

action: Developer: build an enrolment screen with recent sign-in, QR code, manual key and confirmation-code entry.
expected: Only a valid authenticator code completes enrolment. Cancelling leaves enrolment incomplete.

action: Developer: build the authenticator challenge for each supported sign-in route and deploy the changes.
expected: Live sign-in handles the Firebase MFA challenge and reports incorrect codes clearly. The local simulated reviewer is separate from this check.

action: Owner: sign in, scan the setup QR code in an authenticator app and enter its current code. Sign out and sign in again.
expected: Firebase records the factor and the fresh live sign-in requests the authenticator code. Record the account reference and time, without recording the key or codes.

action: Try an incorrect code, a code outside the configured acceptance window and cancelling the challenge.
expected: No completed MFA sign-in and no restricted data. Record the configured acceptance window rather than assuming a code expires immediately at a 30-second boundary.

action: Check operations access while signed out, as an ordinary host and as an authorised reviewer without a completed MFA sign-in. Test the server endpoints as well as the page.
expected: All are denied. The live server requires both the operations role and evidence of a second-factor sign-in. Google-account two-step verification alone is not this evidence.

action: Sign in as the authorised MFA reviewer and open the operations queue, a held case and its photos.
expected: Access succeeds. The incomplete-screening tag and reason are visible where applicable. Opening a case or photo records the reviewer in the audit.

action: Release one disposable memory case, release held feedback and delete a separate disposable case.
expected: Memory goes to host review or renewed screening; feedback goes to the private inbox; deletion hides content and queues file removal. Actions are audited.

action: Verify sign-out, a fresh sign-in after reviewer permissions are withdrawn on a disposable account, and the documented existing-session revocation behaviour.
expected: Signed-out and newly unauthorised sessions are denied. Record any delay or gap for existing sessions instead of assuming immediate revocation.

action: Document the lost-authenticator recovery process and verify it using a disposable reviewer account.
expected: Identify who can perform recovery and verify re-enrolment. Recovery must not provide password-only access to Safety Review. Do not record authenticator keys or codes in the test report.

action: Repeat the supported reviewer journey on mobile and desktop; record each step, evidence and fault in the shared NAS register.
expected: Actual device coverage is marked. Unavailable setup or live checks are recorded as blocked in notes, never as passed.

action: Content reports: Select Content reports and refresh. Using a disposable test memory, submit a clearly labelled test report through the guest reporting flow, then refresh and locate its exact report reference.
expected: The queue loads without an access error. The test report appears with its reference and status. Restricted report text and photos are absent from the overview. Record creation and queue-load results separately if either is blocked.

action: Privacy requests: Select Privacy requests and refresh. Submit a clearly labelled synthetic privacy request through Privacy & Safety using the test contact address, then locate its exact request reference.
expected: The queue loads and the test request appears with reference, status and any applicable review deadline. Do not treat a received request as completed deletion. Record the request ID and receipt/queue evidence.

action: Safety cases: Select Safety cases and refresh. Locate a disposable held memory or private-feedback case from the screening tests, and a screening-incomplete case where available. Open the case; use the existing release/delete tests for decisions.
expected: The queue loads with the expected case references and statuses. Opening permitted case content is audited. Incomplete screening has its reason tagged; content stays private until the approved route permits publication or delivery. Record missing fixtures or unsupported live tagging as pending/faults.

action: Alerts: Select Alerts and refresh. Ask engineering to identify a controlled test alert or create one through the relevant test-only overdue/deadline scenario, then locate its exact reference. Do not age real customer cases to generate an alert.
expected: The queue loads. The known test alert appears with reference, kind and status. Empty queues show No items in this queue. If no test alert exists, queue loading can pass while alert creation/visibility remains pending.

action: Deletion jobs: Select Deletion jobs and refresh. Delete a disposable test memory with uploaded photos using TP-OPS-06, then identify the exact deletion-job reference and refresh after the worker runs.
expected: The queue loads and the expected job/status is visible. Verify each targeted storage object separately under TP-OPS-06; a listed or completed job alone is not proof that files were deleted. Record job ID, timestamps and actual object evidence.

action: Consent deletion reviews: Select Consent deletion reviews and refresh. Identify a disposable consent-review fixture through the retention tests. Click Check consent retention; verify its exact consent path, status and available deadline/action/evidence. If manual deletion is due, use only the authorised disposable fixture and recheck afterward.
expected: The queue loads and the known review appears. The expanded review points to the correct consent record; after authorised deletion, rechecking reflects the actual record state. Do not delete a real guest consent record for this test or claim long-term expiry is automated. If no fixture exists, mark that portion pending.

action: Match the clear controls from TP-GUEST-07-S01, TP-GUEST-09-S05, TP-GUEST-09-S06 to authorised diagnostics by property, submission/revision and screening reference. Check public/in-stay visibility and private-feedback delivery; look for any unexpected safety case.
expected: A clear memory with host review off is visible after screening; feedback is private. Spoof/valid UNKNOWN alone does not create a safety hold. No queue item is expected for a clear submission.

action: Match all ordinary-category submissions from TP-GUEST-08, review-on/contact cases from TP-GUEST-07, and medical/racy cases from TP-GUEST-09. Check the host-review list using each exact reference. Check private feedback separately.
expected: The held memory belongs to the correct host/property and stays off both walls before approval. Ordinary private feedback reaches the host inbox. Operations uses authorised diagnostics to verify non-serious provider categories; they are not expected as restricted safety cases.

action: For every serious text category in TP-GUEST-08 and adult/violence photo category in TP-GUEST-09, find the exact memory or feedback case in Safety Review. Match submission/revision, property, categories and screening reference. Perform the access checks in TP-OPS-04-S03 and TP-OPS-08-S08.
expected: Each serious fixture has a matching restricted case with the observed category. Text cases cover both memory and feedback; photo cases cover memories. Ordinary hosts cannot read case content, release it, or access its restricted photos.

action: Reconcile every category case from TP-GUEST-08 and TP-GUEST-09 against its provider result. Record one line per memory/feedback variation: fixture, submission, revision, category, score/likelihood, actual destination and evidence.
expected: All 16 text categories and all 5 photo categories have observed results or an explicit Needs review / blocked reason. Local markers and isolated responses prove routing only. A real-provider category miss stays outstanding even if application routing follows the returned score.

action: Open every incomplete-screening reference from TP-GUEST-07-S05 and TP-GUEST-09-S07. Verify the tagged reason and private state, then continue TP-OPS-03 with those same references.
expected: Both text routes and the photo-memory route have correctly matched incomplete-screening cases. A retry or host approval cannot silently publish/deliver while a restricted case remains unresolved.

action: Check the combined cases from TP-GUEST-07-S07. Resolve separate disposable ordinary and serious cases using TP-OPS-04-S04 and TP-OPS-08-S09. Keep unresolved cases until their corresponding guest/operations checks are complete.
expected: The strongest restriction wins. A safety release follows the configured host-review/rescreening or private-feedback route. Reviewer decisions are audited; deletion is a separate authorised action with file-removal evidence under TP-OPS-06.

action: Hand the category checklist back to the guest tester. Use the originating TP-GUEST-07, TP-GUEST-08 or TP-GUEST-09 step ID in each operations result and consolidate the paired guest/operations evidence in the shared register.
expected: Every guest fixture has an operations result or explicit pending reason. Guest confirmation alone and a generic loaded queue do not complete the paired test. Record guest outcome and operations outcome separately.
